newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish central bank gives licence to regional bank.
newsitem.headline: Polish central bank gives licence to regional bank.

text.p: The National Bank of Poland on Wednesday granted an operating licence to Baltycki Bank Regionalny SA (BBR), a regional bank grouping 73 co-operative banks in north-west Poland, the central bank president said.
BBR, with a share capital of 15.9 million zlotys, is the sixth regional bank created in Poland under a sweeping reform of the country's ailing small cooperative bank sector.
"Cooperative banks fill an important market niche... the sector best reaches small clients in towns and villages," Hanna Gronkiewicz-Waltz told Reuters after the licence ceremony.

The cooperative bank restructuring scheme envisages the creation of nine regional banks which were subordinated to Bank Gospodarki Zywnosciowej SA (BGZ) grouping 1,200 of the country's 1,600 small cooperative banks.
Before the scheme started two years ago nearly one-thind of the contry's cooperative banks were in danger of bankruptcy after a huge wave of bad loans to farmers in the early 1990s.
